newsitem.title: UK: Copper physical premiums stable, but may ease soon.
newsitem.headline: Copper physical premiums stable, but may ease soon.

text.p: Premiums and discounts remained steady in the European physical copper market, although this may change if the flare-up in LME backwardations continues, traders said.
So far this week, the cash/threes spread on the LME has widened from $45 a tonne to $90, as pressure builds up on late-April/early-May dates.
"If this backwardation widens, then we will see the (physical) premiums ease," one trader said.
A U.S. investment bank was said to be the major long position holder, while an influentual speculator was one of the shorts, some dealers suggested.

So far, the impact on physicals of the latest flare-up in LME tightness has been negligible. However, fierce nearby backwardations eventually dissuade the holding of metal, as it becomes financially more attractive to lend to the market.
As well as the developments in the spread, there are some signs that Chinese interest is picking up beyond the residual regular business.

There have been reports of enquiries circulating in Europe because the premiums in Singapore are reaching expensive levels of some $50. Thus, it may be more feasible to ship copper from Europe, although the lead times are considerably longer.
Also, the seasonal shut down of Russia's Dudinka port because of high water levels will exarcabate any LME tightness as shipments of Norilsk standard cathode supplies dry up, they added.
